item.title: Nerd Show and Tell — Thu Nov 5, 6:00 PM — HackLab.TO 1677 St Clair Ave W
item.description:
It is easier to talk about your projects and what you want to learn than build something that real integrates into people's lives. Either show up and demo what you are building or come over, try what other people are building, give your feedback, get inspired, and learn something. Why talk about what can be when you can be the change you want to see in the world?
​Change requires knowledge, skills, and coordination. With all this information at our fingertips knowing what to ignore is more important than knowing what one should know. My bet is that we can achieve more together than alone.
​So let's get our values articulated, so we can converse, and build a future worth getting excited about!
Source: HackLab.TO

item.title: Wilder Forest/Pleasure Valley, Intermediate Hike — Sat Nov 14, 9:30 AM
item.description:
GTA Hiking & Stuff Join us in an autumn hike at Pleasure Valley/Walker Woods! This will be a longer than normal hike for the GTA Hiking group. We have scheduled the hike for 3 hours but it may take longer to complete depending on how many times we stop. Bring snacks and water to keep the engine running.
The Glen Major Forest is one of the most mature forests within the Durham Regional Forest network. The route follows the wide trails with a very good variety of scenic viewpoints. We will do a large loop enjoying the many rolling hills.
The pace will be moderate, taking breaks along the way. We can adjust as needed. The length of the hike is roughly 10-11 km in 3hrs or more.
Come out and enjoy the crisp fall air and take in some forest bathing.

item.title: La Société d'histoire de Toronto HISTORITOUR - LA JUNCTION - À la croisée des voies ferrées 2ème partie — Sat Nov 14, 1:30 PM — Wallace Avenue Fotbridge
item.description: Départ : À l’arrêt de bus Dundas St West & Glenlake Avenue (bus 40 A, 40 B et 140), à quelques pas du Wallace Footbridge. Arrivée : Arrêt de tramway #505 ou #506 Sterling road and Dundas Guides : Wafa Smiai – Rolande Smith Malgré son nom presque jumeau, Junction Triangle est un quartier distinct de The Junction : né lui aussi du même noeud ferroviaire, mais historiquement rattaché à la ville de West Toronto plutôt qu’à West Toronto Junction. Triangle formé par les voies ferrées du CN/CP à l’ouest, la ligne GO Barrie à l’est, et le faisceau ferroviaire du CP au nord, ce secteur reste aujourd’hui l’un des plus purs témoins du paysage industriel qui a fait naître tout le secteur — Junction comme Junction Triangle. Cette visite reste entièrement dans ce périmètre compact, et racontera une autre facette du même combat patrimonial : moins de bâtiments individuellement classés, mais un tissu industriel entier, et une question récurrente sur qui a le droit de continuer à l’occuper.
